_doc: Courting and proposing. 'ask' lines are YOURS, the rest theirs. Vars: {money} (token), {who} (whose consent is missing). Tags on court.feelings.reply: feel_hostile/cold/neutral/warm/devoted, p_low/p_mid/p_high, needs_consent.

ask: You're looking well today, {first}. Very well.
I've been wanting to tell you: your smile is the best sight in {place}.
Forgive me, {first}, but I can't stop noticing how fair you are.
It's a better {part} for having you in it.
If I'm staring, it's because you're worth staring at.

ask.t: A rose has nothing on you, {first}. Not even in June.
You walk like a lady and laugh like a lark. How is it done?
There's no sweeter voice in the choir, {first}. Or the field.
Strong hands, kind eyes. A lucky woman will be the one who earns them.

ask: Your laugh carries across the whole green, {first}. I find myself listening for it.
It's a better day for seeing you.
I'd stand in the rain to talk with you, {first}.

yes.t: Oh! You're too kind. My cheeks are hot.
Is that so? I'd not have guessed you noticed.
You have a way of saying things, {first}.
Well. That's... pleasing to hear.
I think I shall remember that for a good while.
Ha! Go on. I'll not stop you.
You say the loveliest things.
I'll treasure that, {first}.
Hush — someone will hear. Say it again.

no.t: I think you mistake me, {first}.
You're kind, but I'd rather you spoke plainer.
Please. People are looking.
Do that again and I'll tell my father.
I've work to do, {first}. Save your fancy words.
You flatter me; and I'm unsure of you.
Perhaps. But not just now.
Someone's watching. Be careful.

ask: Would you walk out with me, {first}? Only as far as the green.
It's a fine {part}. Would you take a turn with me?
Might I walk you home, {first}?
I'd like to walk with you a while, if you'll allow it.

ask.t: Come, {first}, the evening is made for a stroll. Will you?
Walk with me to the church and back, after Mass?

ask: Would you let me walk you to the well?
A turn about the green, {first}? Just you and I?
May I keep you company a little way?

yes.t: I'd like that. Give me a moment to fetch my shawl.
Gladly. Not too fast, though; I'd like to talk.
Yes. Let's go the long way round.
Folk will talk, you know. I find I don't mind.
You'll tell me of your day, and I'll tell you of mine.
I'd like that very much.
Come, then. Tell me about your day.
Let's go. The long way, mind.

no.t: Not today, {first}. I'm needed at home.
I'd rather not be seen with you just yet.
Another time, perhaps. I've too much to do.
No. And stop asking.
My mother would not approve.
I'm expected elsewhere, {first}.
Not today. Don't be discouraged.

ask: I bought you this at the fair: a ribbon for your hair. It cost {money}.
A trifle, {first} — a small brooch. It cost {money}, and it's yours.
I thought of you when I saw this. {Money}, but it's yours to keep.
Take it, {first}, as a token of my regard.

ask.t: A comb of horn, {first}. I carved the edge myself. Well — I tried.

ask: A little ribbon, {first} — blue, to match your eyes. {Money}.
I made this for you. It cost me {money} for the cord alone.

yes.t: Oh, {first}. It's beautiful. I shall wear it to Mass.
You shouldn't have. I'm glad you did.
I'll keep it close to my heart, I think.
Not a soul has given me anything like this before.
Well! I'll put it by my bed. You've a good heart.
It's lovely. Thank you.
I'll wear it Sunday... on the holy day.
You are kind to think of me.

no.t: It's very pretty, but I can't take it. People would talk.
Keep it, {first}. I have no wish to be bought.
You mistake my feeling for yours. I'm sorry.
I couldn't. My father would have my hide.
I mustn't. Truly.
It's lovely, but I can't.
Give it to someone it will mean more to.

refuse.t: I'm not free to hear such things, {first}.
You must not say that to me.
That would be improper, and we both know it.
I think we should speak of something else.

ask: Tell me honestly, {first}: how do you think of me?
What do you feel, when we talk?
Do you ever think of me, {first}? Even a little?
I need to know, {first}. Where do I stand with you?

reply.t: I think I'd rather not say, {first}. And that tells you something.
I like you well enough, {first}. Time will tell the rest.
You are a friend, and a good one. Perhaps more, one day.
I look for you when I'm out. I did not expect that.
I think of you more than is wise, {first}.
My heart is yours, {first}, if you want it. I'm nearly sure.
You know how I feel. I could not hide it if I tried.
But there are others to be asked before we say more: {who} must agree.

ask: {First}, will you marry me?
I'd like to ask you something that can't wait: will you be my {spouseword}?
I've thought on this long. Will you have me, {first}?
Let us not wait any longer, {first}. Marry me.

ask.t: Before God and these walls: be my wife, {first}.
Before God and these walls: be my husband, {first}.

yes.t: Yes. Yes! A thousand times yes.
I thought you'd never ask, {first}. Yes.
Then let the banns be read. I'm yours.
Yes, {first}. God and the priest willing, and every neighbour besides.
Yes. I could not have wished for another.
Then it's settled. God send us joy.
Yes, my love. A hundred times.

no.t: I'm sorry, {first}. I... I can't.
It would not be right. I'm so sorry.
No. And I'd thank you not to ask again.
Ask me in a season, {first}. I'm not yet sure.
Not yet. Not you. I'm sorry.
I like you, but I can't.

consent.t: I want it, {first}, but I cannot say yes until {who} agrees. Ask them first.
My heart says yes. But it isn't mine alone to give: {who} must consent.
Speak to {who}, {first}. Without their blessing I can't.

young.t: We are both too young yet, {first}. Wait until we're grown.
Ask me when I'm sixteen. Not before.

later.t: Not yet, {first}. There is still too much we haven't said.
I'm not ready. But I'm not saying no.
Give it time. Court me a little longer.
Ask me again after the harvest.
I'm fond of you. I need more time.
